questions.difficultyReason: Students must identify the zero-normal-force threshold and link it to the largest downward SHM acceleration.

explanation.body: At the top of the motion, the downward force equation is $ma=mg-N$. At the limiting amplitude $N=0$, so $m\omega^2x_0=mg$. Hence $x_0=g/\omega^2=g/(2\pi f)^2=9.81/[4\pi^2(2.0)^2]=6.2\ \mathrm{cm}$ to two significant figures.

questions.stemText: A wooden block is floating on a body of highly viscous liquid. What degree of damping does the block experienced when it is oscillating? A Critical damping. B Heavy damping. C Light damping. D No damping.

appearances.originalFile: grail:10416 ACJC 2023 J2 H2 Physics Prelim P1

questions.difficultyReason: The presence of repeated cycles with decreasing amplitude identifies the damping regime.
questions.misconception: Inferring the damping regime from the liquid’s viscosity alone.

explanation.body: The block completes several oscillations while viscous forces dissipate its mechanical energy. Its amplitude decreases until it is effectively at rest, which is characteristic of light damping.

perOption.A: Critical damping returns the block to equilibrium without repeated oscillations.
perOption.B: Heavy damping gives a slower, nonoscillatory return to equilibrium.
perOption.C: Correct. Oscillations persist while their amplitude decreases.
perOption.D: Without damping, the oscillations would continue at constant amplitude.

questions.difficultyReason: Squaring the SHM speed relation gives the energy ratio directly.

The speed v of the water waves is given by = v gd where g is the acceleration due to gravity and d is the depth of the water in the tank. If the depth of the water in the tank is 0.30 m, what is the wavelength of the water waves when the cork is moving up and down with the largest amplitude? A 0.070 m B 0.14 m C 0.21 m D 0.35 m

appearances.originalFile: ACJC Physics/H2/2026 J2 H2 Physics Prelim P1 sharing.pdf

questions.difficultyReason: Must link resonance to the natural frequency and then combine with a given wave-speed formula.
questions.misconception: Not recognising that maximum amplitude means driving frequency equals natural frequency

explanation.body:
The cork vibrates with maximum amplitude at resonance, when the wave period equals the cork's natural period, $T = 0.12$ s.

perOption.B: Does not follow from $\lambda = vT$ with $v = \sqrt{gd}$.
perOption.C: Correct. Resonance: wave period equals the natural period.
perOption.D: Forgets the square root: $Tgd \approx 0.35$ m.

questions.difficultyReason: Students must read $x_0$ and $v_0$ from the ellipse and realise that constant energy forces $\omega$ to change.
questions.misconception: Assuming the angular frequency stays the same when the amplitude changes

explanation.body:
From the graph, $x_0 = 0.50\ \mathrm{m}$ and $v_0 = 2.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, so $\omega = \dfrac{v_0}{x_0} = \dfrac{2.0}{0.50} = 4.0\ \mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$.

Total energy $E_T = \tfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2 x_0^2$. Since $E_T$ and $m$ are constant, $\omega x_0$ stays constant:

$\omega' x_0' = \omega x_0 \Rightarrow \omega' = \dfrac{4.0 \times 0.50}{0.25} = 8.0\ \mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$

explanation.body: With greater damping, more energy is lost per cycle, so the amplitude of the forced oscillations is lower at all frequencies (the resonance peak is lower and flatter).

perOption.A: Correct. More damping reduces amplitude across the response curve.
perOption.B: Damping removes energy, so it cannot raise the amplitude.
perOption.C: Damping lowers the curve below resonance as well, especially at the peak.
perOption.D: Damping never increases amplitude.

explanation.body: Q's free oscillations die away faster, so Q is more strongly damped. Its frequency-response curve lies below P's at positive driving frequencies, which rules out A and B. Q has a lower peak at a slightly lower frequency than P.
